name: Teach the World Foundation
mission: To revolutionize education for underserved communities around the globe by pioneering innovative solutions to enhance literacy and learning through digital technology.
theoryOfChange: Teach the World Foundation has a published 'Learning Model' which functions as a strategic framework. This model, detailed in a document on GlobalGiving, outlines their mission to use digital, game-based learning technologies to address illiteracy in the developing world. It describes how the model is implemented by facilitators, the use of learning technologies (tablets, game-based applications), and the expected outcomes, such as students outperforming those in traditional classrooms. The organization's website further elaborates on their 'Proof of concept results,' explaining how their model enables children to 'self learn' and 'democratizes' education by providing effective, engaging, and scalable learning solutions.

strengths_deep_dive: Teach the World Foundation leverages digital learning solutions to scale basic education in low-resource environments. Verified testing showed measurable progress in student outcomes, such as gains in <cite id="6">English alphabet reading and math recognition</cite>. Additionally, operational costs remain constrained, with <cite id="9">$0.01 required to raise each dollar</cite> and a direct delivery expense calculated at $7.10 per student served.
rich_narrative.summary:
Founded in 2015, Teach the World Foundation focuses on addressing global illiteracy by deploying digital learning models in underserved communities <cite id="3">including Pakistan, Malawi, and Bangladesh</cite>. The organization uses tablet-based software through its Microschools and InSchool programs to foster self-directed learning <cite id="3">and improve core literacy and math skills</cite>. In FY2024 filings, the foundation reported <cite id="1">Total Revenue of $254,278</cite> alongside an overall <cite id="9">Charity Navigator score of 84.0/100</cite>.

Financial and operational metrics present a balanced profile. The foundation operates with a <cite id="9">high fundraising efficiency, spending $0.02 per $1 raised</cite>, and achieves a low per-beneficiary delivery cost. However, the filed <cite id="1">Program Expense Ratio stands at 78.0%</cite>, which is below the 75% industry standard and the <cite id="9">peer median of 89.5%</cite>. Furthermore, liquidity remains limited with approximately 1.5 months of working capital on hand. The organization holds a <cite id="9">Gold Seal of Transparency</cite> and maintains a documented theory of change, while board size remains small with three members.
